correctness.rationale: For p=average(r), constant m=p is distinct from nonconstant r and its sliding period mean is p, so both mean payoffs in the strict Definition 1a Eq(6) equal p^T A p for every invasion epsilon. Nearby m_eta=(1-eta)r+eta p has same period mean p, lies in simplex, differs from r, tends to it uniformly and ties Definition 1c Eq(9). For an actual autonomous replicator cycle the positive support is time-independent, and integrating d log r_i/dt=(Ar)_i-r^TAr yields (Ap)_i=c on support; p^T A p=c; hence p is stationary and global counter-mutant is genuine replicator trajectory. These exact algebraic arguments hold for arbitrary real A without simulation. Limit: nearby interpolants need not be trajectories, but literal Definition 1c quantifies over mutant state sequences.
